answer: In an AI market, each identity is a vertex in a registry and must lock $100 of collateral for 90 days before bidding on jobs, including tending a violet garden. Each deposit permits only one active bid, and the same funds cannot back multiple identities. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore requires locking $100,000. Splitting into aliases creates no extra bidding capacity per dollar, while the lock imposes financing and opportunity costs.
